text: Fill in the missing term in each sentence about β-hCG and prenatal screening.
questions: For an initial β-hCG below 1,500 mIU/mL, the expected minimum 48-hour rise in a potentially viable intrauterine pregnancy is approximately *49:Recall the minimum percentage rise over 48 hours when the initial β-hCG is below 1,500 mIU/mL; doubling is not required.* percent.

The β-hCG level above which an intrauterine gestational sac is generally expected on transvaginal ultrasound is called the *discriminatory:What is the name for the β-hCG threshold that aids scan interpretation?* level, traditionally 1,500 to 2,000 mIU per mL.

Prenatal screening markers are reported as multiples of the *median:What statistical measure standardises the marker values?* for gestational age, not as absolute values, so results are comparable across laboratories.

The fourth analyte in the quadruple screen, not present in the triple test, is *inhibin:Which marker was added to AFP, unconjugated oestriol and hCG to form the quadruple test?* A, whose raised level increases the detection rate for Down syndrome.

overallFeedback.feedback: Expected minimum 48-hour rises vary with the starting hCG concentration: approximately 49%, 40% and 33% as the starting value rises; serial hCG alone cannot establish viability or location. The discriminatory level (traditionally 1,500-2,000 mIU/mL, with a conservative threshold up to 3,500) is the level above which an intrauterine sac is generally expected on transvaginal ultrasound — it aids scan interpretation, but symptoms may need assessment at any hCG level, and an inconclusive scan requires follow-up rather than a single confirmatory reading. Multiples of the median standardise screening across laboratories and gestational ages, and inhibin A completes the quadruple test to improve detection of trisomy 21.
